blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Highlights prominent personalities directly associated with the city of Chandigarh.
Consolidates essential information into a one-line quick facts compendium for fast recall.
Provides structured quick revision points optimized for competitive exam preparation.

cells: Championed the idea of Chandigarh as a new, modern capital; called it a city 'unfettered by the traditions of the past'
American architect-planner; produced Chandigarh's original 1949–50 fan-shaped master plan with Matthew Nowicki
Polish architect who co-designed the original master plan with Mayer; died in a 1950 plane crash, ending the Mayer plan
Swiss-French modernist master architect; redesigned Chandigarh's grid-iron master plan from 1951 and personally designed the Capitol Complex

Le Corbusier's cousin and close collaborator; designed extensively across residential sectors and Panjab University; lived in Chandigarh for over a decade; his furniture designs are now globally prized
British architect couple who designed much of the city's housing and civic buildings
Self-taught outsider artist; secretly built the Rock Garden from industrial/household waste from 1957, opened to the public in 1976
Current (2026) Governor of Punjab and ex-officio Administrator of Chandigarh, since 31 July 2024
Current (since 2024) Lok Sabha MP from Chandigarh, Indian National Congress

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: Distinguish carefully between the two architectural eras — Mayer/Nowicki's discontinued fan-shaped plan (1949–50) versus Le Corbusier's adopted grid-iron plan (from 1951) — a frequently confused sequence.

items: Area ≈114 sq km; borders ONLY Punjab (west/north) and Haryana (east/south); 1 district for the whole UT.
Located at the foothills of the Shivalik Hills, between the Sutlej and Yamuna plains.
Sukhna Choe (seasonal stream) dammed to form Sukhna Lake.
Built to replace Lahore as Punjab's capital after Partition (1947); Shimla was the interim capital, 1947–53.
Name from Chandi Mandir temple + 'garh' (fort/abode).
Planners: Mayer & Nowicki (fan-shaped plan, discontinued 1950) → Le Corbusier (grid-iron plan, from 1951).
1 November 1966: Punjab Reorganisation Act creates Haryana; Chandigarh becomes a UT and joint capital of both states.
1985 Rajiv Gandhi–Longowal Accord proposed transferring Chandigarh to Punjab by 26 Jan 1986 — never implemented.
India's first fully planned post-Independence city; nicknamed 'The City Beautiful'.
Grid of numbered (not named) Sectors, each self-contained.
Body metaphor: Head=Capitol Complex, Heart=Sector 17, Lungs=Leisure Valley, Hand=Open Hand Monument, Circulatory system=roads.
'7 Vs' road hierarchy: V1 (fast highway) to V7 (pedestrian/cycle path).
Capitol Complex — UNESCO World Heritage Site since July 2016 (part of a global 17-site Le Corbusier serial listing across 7 countries).
Open Hand Monument = Chandigarh's official emblem.
No Legislative Assembly; no separate Lieutenant Governor — administered by the Governor of Punjab as ex-officio Administrator (since 1 June 1984).
Current (2026) Administrator: Gulab Chand Kataria. Current MP: Manish Tewari (INC).
Punjab & Haryana High Court, Chandigarh, serves both states plus the UT.
Municipal Corporation of Chandigarh (MCC), est. 1994; Mayor's post rotates annually.
Services-dominated economy; among India's highest per-capita-income UTs/states.
'Tricity' = Chandigarh + Panchkula (Haryana) + Mohali/SAS Nagar (Punjab).
Chandigarh International Airport is located in Mohali, Punjab — not inside the UT.
Population ≈10.55 lakh (2011); literacy ≈86.4%; sex ratio ≈818 (among India's lowest); ≈97% urban.
Panjab University (est. 1882, Lahore) and PGIMER (est. 1962) are the UT's flagship institutions.
Questions on key personalities linked to Chandigarh are repeatedly tested in regional competitive examinations.
One-liner quick facts are primary targets for direct multiple-choice questions (MCQs).
Quick revision points are designed for high-yield, last-minute score enhancement.
Sukhna Lake: Ramsar Site proposal approved by the State Wetland Authority in Sept 2025 — final international designation still pending, so don't call it a confirmed Ramsar site yet.
Zakir Hussain Rose Garden — one of Asia's largest rose gardens.
Rock Garden (Nek Chand) — built secretly from 1957, opened to the public in 1976.
Revise this chapter last — it consolidates every numeric/name fact from Chapters 1–10 in one place for rapid recall.
Cross-check the sequence Mayer/Nowicki → Le Corbusier, and the 1 November 1966 UT-formation date — these are the two most frequently tested history/polity facts.
Always verify current officeholders (Administrator, MP, Mayor) closer to your exam date, since these can change — the Mayor's post in particular rotates annually.
